newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen falling on Lebed sacking.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen falling on Lebed sacking.

text.p: Russian shares, hit by Kremlin political infighting on Thursday, are likely to fall further on Friday after President Boris Yeltsin sacked his maverick national security chief, dealers and analysts said.
Some market players said prices could rise on Yeltsin's show of strength but said the direction of the market would depend on Lebed's detailed reaction to his dismissal.
Most leading Russian stocks fell on Thursday after Interior Minister Alexander Kulikov accused Lebed of plotting a creeping coup and unnerved investors.
Yeltsin, who is preparing for heart surgery, announced on television that he was sacking Lebed. The broadcast was aired after Russian markets had officially closed.
The RTS-24 index of 24 leading stocks fell 2.50 percent to 177.81 on Thursday.
Utility Unified Energy System fell to $0.078 from $0.0822 at Wednesday's close. Mosenergo, another bellwether stock, fell to $0.954 from $0.976. Oil giant LUKoil slid to $9.95 from $10.26.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Jim Nail said one view had it that Lebed's sacking removed uncertainty.

But he added: "My view is that it is bad because it reduces the consensus supporting the current government and eliminates the government's most popular member and risks a renewed flare-up of the Chechen conflict.
"I would be selling now if I were a trader," he said.

Head trader Nick Mokhoff at Alliance-Menatep said Western markets appeared to have viewed the sacking positively as a resolution to a problem which has unsettled markets for weeks. But he said it would be necessary to wait for Lebed's reaction.
"At this level and with this uncertainty, I would not be long in this market. We still have to see how Lebed is going to react to this," he said.
Rinaco-Plus trader Alexander Lobanov said prices fell about half a percent after the Russian Trading System officially closed.
"Foreign investors think it is bad for Russia, as it increases instablity and systemic risk. The market will continue falling until (Yeltsin's) operation."
"Now those with long positions are going through a difficult time as prices will no longer rise."

But Troika-Dialog head of fixed income Robert Devane said: "The market is really reacting more on whether Yeltsin is in or out. What we just saw was the most significant show of Yeltsin's presence in the last couple of months."
